qe:
Statements: A ≥ B = C ; B < D > F ; D ≤ E
Conclusions: I. A = C, II. B = F, III. D = E, IV. B < E, V. F > E
(i) How many conclusions are 100% true?
(ii) How many conclusions are there that are likely to be true (possibility)?
(iii) How many conclusions are 100% false?
qh:
कथन: A ≥ B = C ; B < D > F ; D ≤ E
निष्कर्ष: I. A = C, II. B = F, III. D = E, IV. B < E, V. F > E
(i) कितने निष्कर्ष 100% सत्य हैं?
(ii) कितने निष्कर्ष ऐसे हैं जिनके सत्य होने की संभावना है?
(iii) कितने निष्कर्ष 100% असत्य हैं?
oe: (i) Only IV; (ii) Only I, II and III; (iii) Only V
(i) Only II; (ii) Only I and IV; (iii) Only III
(i) Only IV; (ii) Only II and III; (iii) Only I
(i) Only I; (ii) Only IV and V; (iii) Only II
oh: (i) Only IV; (ii) Only I, II and III; (iii) Only V
(i) Only II; (ii) Only I and IV; (iii) Only III
(i) Only IV; (ii) Only II and III; (iii) Only I
(i) Only I; (ii) Only IV and V; (iii) Only II
e:
Method 1 (Definite, Possibility, and 100% False Breakdown Shortcut):
Step 1: Check Conclusion IV (B to E):
- B < D ≤ E.
- Priority rule: '<' aur '≤' me high priority '<' ko milti hai, atah definite relation $B < E$ banta hai.
- Yeh 100% true conclusion hai (Only IV is 100% true).
Step 2: Check Likely to be True (Possibilities):
- Conclusion I (A = C): $A \ge B = C \implies A \ge C$. Chuki $A \ge C$ definite hai, isliye $A = C$ ki sambhavna (possibility) satya hai.
- Conclusion II (B = F): B se F tak $B < D > F$ me condition block banti hai (no definite relation). Block sthiti me $B = F$ ki possibility satya hoti hai.
- Conclusion III (D = E): $D \le E$ definite hai, isliye $D = E$ ki possibility satya hai.
- Atah I, II, aur III likely to be true hain.
Step 3: Check 100% False:
- Conclusion V (F > E): F se E tak relation dekhein: $F < D \le E \implies F < E$ definite satya hai.
- Jab $F < E$ 100% satya hai, toh $F > E$ purna roop se asambhav (100% false) hai.
Atah '(i) Only IV; (ii) Only I, II and III; (iii) Only V' sahi hai.

Method 2 (Sign Verification):
Definite true = IV ($B < E$). Possibilities = I, II, III. 100% False = V ($F > E$, kyunki $F < E$ hai).
Sahi uttar '(i) Only IV; (ii) Only I, II and III; (iii) Only V' hai.

Exam point: kathan-nishkarsh ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe:
Statement: P ≥ R = T ≤ S
Conclusions: I. P > T, II. P = T, III. S ≥ R
qh:
कथन: P ≥ R = T ≤ S
निष्कर्ष: I. P > T, II. P = T, III. S ≥ R
oe: Only either I or II and III follow
oh: Only either I or II and III follow
e:
Method 1 (Either-Or & Definite Truth Shortcut):
Step 1: P se T tak ka definite sambandh nikalein: $P \ge R = T \implies P \ge T$.
- Chuki $P \ge T$ ka arth hai $P > T$ ya $P = T$, isliye Conclusion I ($P > T$) aur Conclusion II ($P = T$) me 'Either I or II' ka sambandh banega.
Step 2: S se R tak dekhein: $R = T \le S \implies R \le S$, jise ulatne par $S \ge R$ banta hai.
- Atah Conclusion III ($S \ge R$) 100% nishchit satya hai (Follows).
Step 3: Final nishkarsh: 'Only either I or II and III follow'.
Correct option  hai.

Method 2 (Sign Splitting Method):
$P \ge T$ do sambhavnaon '>' aur '=' me split hota hai (Either I or II). $S \ge R$ statement se seedhe sidhh hota hai. Atah 'Only either I or II and III follow' sahi hai.

Exam point: kathan-nishkarsh ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

(ii) निष्कर्ष: I. R < T, II. R = T
(iii) निष्कर्ष: I. P > Y, II. P ≤ Y
oe: (i) Either I or II, (ii) Either I or II, (iii) Either I or II
(i) Only I follows, (ii) Only II follows, (iii) None follows
(i) Either I or II, (ii) Only I follows, (iii) None follows
(i) Only II follows, (ii) Either I or II, (iii) Either I or II
oh: (i) Either I or II, (ii) Either I or II, (iii) Either I or II

e:
Method 1 (Either-Or Triad Shortcut Rules):
Step 1: Sub-question (i): M se S tak $M \ge R = S \implies M \ge S$.
- Definite relation '≥' hone ke karan '>' aur '=' ke beech 'Either I or II follows' banega.
Step 2: Sub-question (ii): R se T tak $R = S \le T \implies R \le T$.
- Definite relation '≤' hone ke karan '<' aur '=' ke beech 'Either I or II follows' banega.
Step 3: Sub-question (iii): P se Y tak $P > W < Y$.
- Viprit chinh aane se condition block banta hai (no relation).
- Jab no relation ho aur dono nishkarshon me teeno chinh ($>$, $<$, $=$) upasthit hon ($P > Y$ aur $P \le Y$), toh 'Either I or II follows' banta hai.
Atah teeno me 'Either I or II follows' lagu hota hai.
Correct option  hai.

Method 2 (Case Matching):
Har sub-question do complementary situations ko cover karta hai jo exhaustive hain. Atah sabhi me Either-Or banta hai.
Sahi uttar '(i) Either I or II, (ii) Either I or II, (iii) Either I or II' hai.

Exam point: kathan-nishkarsh ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe:
Statements: R ≥ U = P ; S ≥ T = M ; P > Y < W
Conclusions: I. U < W, II. R < P, III. R = P
qh:
कथन: R ≥ U = P ; S ≥ T = M ; P > Y < W
निष्कर्ष: I. U < W, II. R < P, III. R = P
e:
Method 1 (Condition Block & Sign Mismatch Shortcut):
Step 1: Conclusion I ($U < W$): U se W tak $U = P > Y < W$. Viprit chinh ('>' aur '<') aane ke karan condition block banta hai, atah koi sambandh nahi banta (False).
Step 2: R aur P ke beech relation: $R \ge U = P \implies R \ge P$.
- Iska arth hai ki ya toh $R > P$ hoga ya $R = P$.
- Conclusion II me $R < P$ diya gaya hai (jo asambhav hai) aur Conclusion III me $R = P$ diya hai.
- Chuki Either-Or banne ke liye '>' aur '=' chahiye the, jabki yahan '<' diya hai, isliye Either-Or nahi banega.
Atah koi bhi nishkarsh follow nahi karta.
Correct option  None follows hai.

Method 2 (Sign Verification):
$R \ge P$ me '<' ka astitva nahi ho sakta. U aur W me block hai. Atah None follows sahi hai.
Sahi uttar 'None follows' hai.

Exam point: kathan-nishkarsh ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe:
Statements: R ≥ U = P ; S ≥ T = M ; P > Y < W
Conclusions: I. S > M, II. M = S
qh:
कथन: R ≥ U = P ; S ≥ T = M ; P > Y < W
निष्कर्ष: I. S > M, II. M = S
e:
Method 1 (Direct '≥' Either-Or Shortcut Trick):
Step 1: S se M tak ka sambandh statement se dekhein: $S \ge T = M \implies S \ge M$.
Step 2: $S \ge M$ ka arth hota hai ki ya toh $S > M$ hoga ya $S = M$.
- Conclusion I: $S > M$
- Conclusion II: $M = S \equiv S = M$
Step 3: Dono nishkarsh milkar poore '≥' relation ko cover karte hain.
Atah 'Either I or II follows' banta hai.
Correct option  Either I or II follows hai.

Method 2 (Complementary Verification):
$S \ge M$ me kewal do hi sambhavnaayein hain: bada ya barabar. Dono nishkarsh me maujood hain, isliye Either-Or sahi hai.
Sahi uttar 'Either I or II follows' hai.

Exam point: kathan-nishkarsh ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe:
Statements: R ≥ U = P ; S ≥ T = M ; P > Y < W
Conclusions: I. M < S, II. M = S
qh:
कथन: R ≥ U = P ; S ≥ T = M ; P > Y < W
निष्कर्ष: I. M < S, II. M = S
e:
Method 1 (Reverse Direction '≤' Shortcut Trick):
Step 1: Statement se M se S tak ka sambandh nikalein: $M = T \le S \implies M \le S$.
Step 2: $M \le S$ ka spasht arth hai: ya toh $M < S$ hoga ya $M = S$.
- Conclusion I: $M < S$
- Conclusion II: $M = S$
Step 3: Dono me se kisi ek ka satya hona anivarya hai.
Atah 'Either I or II follows' nikalta hai.
Correct option  Either I or II follows hai.

Method 2 (Sign Decomposition):
'≤' chinh '<' aur '=' se milkar bana hai. Dono prashn me diye gaye hain, atah Either I or II lagu hota hai.
Sahi uttar 'Either I or II follows' hai.

Exam point: kathan-nishkarsh ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe:
Statements: R ≥ U = P ; S ≥ T = M ; P > Y < W
Conclusions: I. P < R, II. R = P, III. R > Y
qh:
कथन: R ≥ U = P ; S ≥ T = M ; P > Y < W
निष्कर्ष: I. P < R, II. R = P, III. R > Y
oe: Only Either I or II and III follow
oh: Only Either I or II and III follow
e:
Method 1 (Combined Independent True & Either-Or Shortcut):
Step 1: P aur R ke beech relation: $R \ge U = P \implies R \ge P \implies P \le R$.
- $P \le R$ ka matlab hai ya toh $P < R$ ya $P = R$.
- Atah Conclusion I ($P < R$) aur Conclusion II ($R = P$) ke beech 'Either I or II' banega.
Step 2: R aur Y ke beech relation: $R \ge U = P > Y \implies R > Y$.
- High priority sign '>' hone ke karan Conclusion III ($R > Y$) 100% nishchit satya hai (Follows).
Step 3: Dono ko milane par: 'Only Either I or II and III follow'.
Correct option  hai.

Method 2 (Priority & Decomposition Check):
$R > Y$ direct statement se satya hai. $P \le R$ se Either I or II satya hai. Sahi vikalp  hai.

Exam point: kathan-nishkarsh ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe:
Statements: A ≥ B = C ; E ≤ F = G ; C > Z < D
Evaluate the following conclusion pairs:
Ex25. Conclusions: I. C > D, II. C ≤ D
Ex26. Conclusions: I. C ≥ D, II. C < D
Ex27. Conclusions: I. C > D, II. D ≥ C
qh:
कथन: A ≥ B = C ; E ≤ F = G ; C > Z < D
निम्नलिखित निष्कर्ष युग्मों का मूल्यांकन कीजिए:
Ex25. निष्कर्ष: I. C > D, II. C ≤ D
Ex26. निष्कर्ष: I. C ≥ D, II. C < D
Ex27. निष्कर्ष: I. C > D, II. D ≥ C
oe: Ex25: Either, Ex26: Neither, Ex27: Either
Ex25: Either, Ex26: Either, Ex27: Neither
All three (Ex25, Ex26, Ex27) are Either I or II follows
oh: Ex25: Either, Ex26: Neither, Ex27: Either
Ex25: Either, Ex26: Either, Ex27: Neither
All three (Ex25, Ex26, Ex27) are Either I or II follows
e:
Method 1 (3-Sign Condition Block Either-Or Shortcut):
Step 1: C aur D ke beech relation dekhein: $C > Z < D$. Viprit chinh ('>' aur '<') aane ke karan Condition Block banta hai (no relation).
Step 2: Rule: Condition Block hone par yadi dono nishkarshon me teeno chinh ($>$, $<$, $=$) shamil hon aur subject-object samaan hon, toh 'Either-Or' lagu hota hai:
- Ex25: I. $C > D$ aur II. $C \le D$ ($<$ aur $=$). Teeno chinh maujood hain $\implies$ Either I or II follows.
- Ex26: I. $C \ge D$ ($>$ aur $=$) aur II. $C < D$. Teeno chinh maujood hain $\implies$ Either I or II follows.
- Ex27: I. $C > D$ aur II. $D \ge C \equiv C \le D$ ($<$ aur $=$). Teeno chinh maujood hain $\implies$ Either I or II follows.
Atah teeno me 'Either I or II follows' lagu hota hai.
Correct option  hai.

Method 2 (Exhaustive Possibility Method):
Do anjaan tatvon me keval 3 sambhavnaayein ($>$, $<$, $=$) ho sakti hain. Teeno questions me ye 3 sambhavnaayein poori tarah cover hoti hain, isliye sabhi me Either-Or banta hai.
Sahi uttar 'All three (Ex25, Ex26, Ex27) are Either I or II follows' hai.

Exam point: kathan-nishkarsh ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe:

Evaluate the following conclusion pairs:

Ex29. Conclusions: I. C = D, II. C ≠ D
Ex30. Conclusions: I. C > D, II. C < D
qh:
कथन: A ≥ B = C ; E ≤ F = G ; C > Z < D
निम्नलिखित निष्कर्ष युग्मों का मूल्यांकन कीजिए:
Ex28. निष्कर्ष: I. C > D, II. D ≤ C
Ex29. निष्कर्ष: I. C = D, II. C ≠ D
Ex30. निष्कर्ष: I. C > D, II. C < D
oe: Ex28: None follows, Ex29: Either I or II follows, Ex30: None follows
Ex28: Either, Ex29: Either, Ex30: Either
Ex28: None follows, Ex29: None follows, Ex30: Either
Ex28: Either, Ex29: None follows, Ex30: None follows
oh: Ex28: None follows, Ex29: Either I or II follows, Ex30: None follows
Ex28: Either, Ex29: Either, Ex30: Either
Ex28: None follows, Ex29: None follows, Ex30: Either
Ex28: Either, Ex29: None follows, Ex30: None follows
e:
Method 1 (3-Sign Check for Condition Block Shortcut):
Step 1: C aur D ke beech condition block hai, atah teeno chinh ($>$, $<$, $=$) anivarya hain.
Step 2: Evaluate Ex28:
- I. $C > D$, II. $D \le C \equiv C \ge D$ ($>$ aur $=$). Yahan '<' chinh gayab hai (kewal $>$ aur $=$ hain). Atah Either-Or nahi banega $\implies$ None follows.
Step 3: Evaluate Ex29:
- I. $C = D$, II. $C \ne D$ (arthath $C > D$ ya $C < D$). Yahan '=' aur '$>$ ya $<$' teeno chinh milkar poora set banate hain. Atah $\implies$ Either I or II follows.
Step 4: Evaluate Ex30:
- I. $C > D$, II. $C < D$. Yahan '=' chinh anupasthit hai. Atah Either-Or nahi banega $\implies$ None follows.
Correct option  hai.

Method 2 (Sign Completeness Rule):
Ex28 me '<' missing hai aur Ex30 me '=' missing hai, isliye dono me None follows. Ex29 me '=' aur '≠' (dono inequalities) milkar 100% domain cover karte hain, isliye Either-Or banta hai.
Sahi uttar 'Ex28: None follows, Ex29: Either I or II follows, Ex30: None follows' hai.

Exam point: kathan-nishkarsh ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe:
Statement: P ≥ R = T ≥ S
Conclusions: I. P > T, II. P = R, III. R ≥ S
qh:
कथन: P ≥ R = T ≥ S
निष्कर्ष: I. P > T, II. P = R, III. R ≥ S
oe: Either I or II and III follow
oh: Either I or II and III follow
e:
Method 1 (Interchangeable Elements Either-Or Shortcut):
Step 1: Statement me $R = T$ diya gaya hai.
- Conclusion I me $P > T$ ko $P > R$ likha ja sakta hai.
- Conclusion II $P = R$ hai.
Step 2: P se R tak ka sambandh: $P \ge R$.
- $P \ge R$ do bhagon me tootta hai: $P > R$ (Conclusion I) ya $P = R$ (Conclusion II).
- Atah I aur II ke beech 'Either I or II follows' banega.
Step 3: Conclusion III: $R = T \ge S \implies R \ge S$ direct statement se 100% satya hai.
Step 4: Atah 'Either I or II and III follow' sahi hai.
Correct option  hai.

Method 2 (Equivalent Substitution):
$R = T$ hone se $P > T \equiv P > R$. $P \ge R$ hone ke karan I aur II me Either-Or banta hai, aur $R \ge S$ nishchit satya hai. Sahi vikalp  hai.

Exam point: kathan-nishkarsh ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe:
Statements: M = N ≥ P ; P = R ≥ S ; R > U
Conclusions: I. M > R, II. N = P, III. P > U
qh:
कथन: M = N ≥ P ; P = R ≥ S ; R > U
निष्कर्ष: I. M > R, II. N = P, III. P > U
oe: None of these (Either I or II and III follow)
oh: None of these (Either I or II and III follow)
e:
Method 1 (Substitution & Priority Evaluation Shortcut):
Step 1: Statements me $M = N$ aur $P = R$ diya gaya hai.
- Iska arth hai ki Conclusion I ($M > R$) ko $N > P$ likha ja sakta hai.
- Conclusion II $N = P$ hai.
Step 2: N aur P ka definite relation: $N \ge P$.
- $N \ge P$ ka arth hai ya toh $N > P$ (Conclusion I) ya $N = P$ (Conclusion II).
- Atah I aur II ke beech 'Either I or II' ka sambandh banta hai.
Step 3: P aur U ka relation: $P = R > U \implies P > U$ 100% nishchit satya hai (Conclusion III follows).
Step 4: Atah sahi nishkarsh 'Either I or II and III follow' banta hai, jo diye gaye aam options A, B, C, D me nahi hai.
Correct option  None of these hai.

Method 2 (Box & Chain Method):
III satya hai aur I tatha II milkar $N \ge P$ poora karte hain. Isliye Either I or II and III follow hoga.
Sahi uttar 'None of these (Either I or II and III follow)' hai.

Exam point: kathan-nishkarsh ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.
